headline: WHEAT BREAKS 3.4%; SEPTEMBER WASDE LOOMS
subheadline: Black Sea peace-talk headlines hit wheat hard; soybean oil drops on the crush split; corn eases into harvest.
lead: Wheat dropped 25 cents to $7.16 on Black Sea peace-talk headlines that pulled the geopolitical premium out of the winter crop in one session. Corn gave back another 3.5 cents to $5.37 December, a fourth losing day running as harvest pressure builds. The September WASDE next Thursday at 11 AM CT is the next real number that resets every story in this complex.
the_takeaway: Wheat's geopolitical premium left the building today; hold new grain and wait for Thursday's WASDE.
teaser: Wheat dropped 25 cents on Black Sea peace talk; corn slips into harvest. Thursday's WASDE decides what comes next.

one_number.unit: US beef export value gain in July vs year-ago
one_number.context: July beef exports rose 6% in value even as China's technical barriers held. Pork fell on a PRV outbreak impact in Mexico. Beef demand offshore is firming, but the gains aren't reaching the live cattle board today.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called corn down toward $4.99; December corn closed $5.37 today, nowhere near that level.
yesterdays_call.note: Corn fell but harvest pressure is pulling it slowly; the $4.99 target was too far in one session.

sections.title: WHEAT BREAKS ON PEACE TALKS
sections.body:
- Chicago wheat tumbled 25 cents to **$7.16**, the biggest single-session loss in weeks, as Black Sea peace-talk headlines pulled the war premium out of the winter crop in one afternoon.
- The move is clean: no change in US crop conditions, no fresh USDA data, just geopolitical risk deflating fast when a diplomatic signal hits a market that had been pricing conflict-driven supply disruption.
- The FAO Food Price Index also rose in August on Black Sea trade logistics concerns, so the board was priced for tension that the headlines just partially removed.
sections.catalyst: Black Sea peace-talk headlines removed geopolitical supply-disruption premium from wheat.
sections.bottom_line: If peace talks stall or reverse, that 25-cent premium comes back just as fast.
sections.vs_yesterday: Wheat: broke lower again, now down two sessions on geopolitical deflation.

sections.title: CORN GRINDS LOWER INTO HARVEST
sections.body:
- December corn settled at **$5.37**, off 3.5 cents, a fourth straight losing session as combines roll in the early Belt and harvest-pressure selling builds.
- Thursday's export sales didn't provide cover: the number wasn't strong enough to offset the weight of fresh bushels hitting country elevators.
- CPKC just reported a record start to its crop year, meaning rail movement is moving early volume fast, which keeps basis from firming the way it might if logistics were tight.
sections.catalyst: Harvest pressure and record CPKC rail crop-year start keeping new-crop supply moving briskly.
sections.bottom_line: Thursday's WASDE is the next real floor test; without a yield surprise, $5.37 is a ceiling, not a floor.
sections.farmer_action: Unpriced December corn above $5.37: the September WASDE on the 11th is your window. Don't assume the price holds there if USDA confirms a big crop.

sections.title: SOYBEAN OIL LEADS CRUSH SPLIT
sections.body:
- Nearby soybeans eased to **$12.94**, off 14 cents, but the story is soybean oil dropping 3.3% while meal held flat -- a sharp reversal of the oil-share narrative that ran all week.
- When oil falls and meal holds, crush economics shift toward meal volume; biofuel-linked oil demand is getting second-guessed after the EPA small-refinery exemption headlines earlier this week.
- Funds are still long November beans at **$13.10**; next Thursday's export sales number is the trigger -- a miss below 300K MT is the first real test of that position.
sections.bottom_line: Meal is carrying the beans right now; if oil can't recover its share, the crush bid for soybeans gets softer heading into WASDE.

sections.title: ENERGY HOLDS; DIESEL CRACK STORY CONTINUES
sections.body:
- WTI crude eased to **$91.22**, off less than a dollar, a quiet session by crude standards even as Brent is being pushed toward $95 by diesel crack spreads at elevated levels.
- The story is refined products, not crude: middle distillate tightness is running diesel margins wide, which is the input-cost story for fall fieldwork and harvest fuel budgets.
- The Iran-Hormuz cycle, a July re-escalation that has since cooled with the premium deflating into August, is no longer the driver; diesel cracks are.
sections.catalyst: Record diesel crack spreads and tightening middle distillate supplies pushing Brent toward $95, per EIA and oilprice.com.
sections.bottom_line: Budget fall harvest fuel now; diesel at wide cracks is a cost the September crop budget doesn't have room for.

outside_the_pit.title: Congress Bill Seeks to Reverse Trump Beef Import Order
outside_the_pit.body: Rep. Figures introduced the Protecting American Beef Producers Act to nullify the Trump beef import proclamation. If it advances, it removes one supply-pressure headwind that has been sitting on cattle prices since the import headlines hit last week.

outside_the_pit.title: EPA and Army Reopen WOTUS Comment Period on New Options
outside_the_pit.body: A supplemental proposed rule on the Waters of the US definition is open for input, with agencies evaluating new regulatory options. For producers with drainage tile, wetland easements, or field-border water features, the final rule sets the compliance map for the next decade.

weekly_thread.question: Will today's Crop Progress rating confirm the August yield cuts or add a weather premium back into corn and beans?
weekly_thread.status_text: The week's crop ratings held steady without a weather surprise, so no premium was added; the September WASDE at 11 AM CT Thursday delivers the definitive answer.

the_more_you_know.title: Black Sea Peace Talks and the Wheat Premium: How Fast It Unwinds
the_more_you_know.body: Wheat carries a geopolitical risk premium when conflict disrupts Black Sea shipping lanes. When diplomatic signals arrive, that premium doesn't bleed out gradually, it reprices in a session, exactly as today's 25-cent drop shows. The floor below that premium is US and EU supply fundamentals, currently not supportive of $7.16 without the war risk.

watch_list.desc: Weekly export sales: soybeans under 300K MT keeps funds in the driver's seat and the November contract vulnerable below $13.00.
September WASDE: corn yield above 181 bu/acre reopens the downside toward $5.20 December; a yield cut below 180 adds a weather premium back.
USDA Crop Progress: harvest pace above 10% nationally means harvest pressure continues; a slow number could provide temporary support.
Black Sea peace-talk follow-through: any breakdown in talks returns wheat's geopolitical premium toward $7.40; a formal agreement removes it entirely.

daily_quote.text: Sell down to the sleeping point.
